newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Caterpillar Q1 EPS seen up about 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Caterpillar Q1 EPS seen up about 10 pct.

text.p: Caterpillar Inc is expected to post an earnings per share gain of about 10 percent for the first quarter, based on strong overall production and a stronger market for U.S. truck engines than expected.

The mean estimate of analysts surveyed by First Call is for $1.69 a share, up from $1.53 a share a year ago, with estimates ranging from $1.50 to $1.85. The heavy equipment maker is scheduled to report earnings before the market opens Tuesday.
J. Blair Brumley, analyst at Dain Bosworth Inc, is calling for earnings of $1.80 a share, based on conditions being better than Peoria, Illinois-based Caterpillar's previous forecast.

"They told you that the heavy duty truck market was going to be down and that's not the case," Brumley said. "Unless Cat is losing a lot of share, that business is going to be a lot better than people put into their (earnings) models."

Stronger than expected economic factors should help earnings this year, if they continue, analysts said. In January, Caterpillar forecast 1997 profits near the 1996 level of $1.4 billion or $7.07 a share.
Analysts think those estimates will prove conservative, as did the company's initial estimates for 1996.
"We expect Caterpillar will throw the towel in on their (conservative) forecasts earlier this year," Thomas Burns Jr., analyst at NatWest Securities Corp said.
One factor that could hurt Caterpillar's earnings, though, is the strength of the dollar, which is at multi-year highs against both the yen and the mark.
About half of Caterpillar's sales are outside the United States.

But Burns said Caterpillar is yet to see a trend of having a pricing disadvantage because of currency factors and Caterpillar said the stronger dollar helped machinery and engine profits in 1996 by reducing yen and European currency-based costs.
